query_text: Have any new literary genres emerged in this century?

action.query: 21st century new literary genres cli-fi litRPG twitterature bizarro fiction new sincerity autofiction
queries: 21st century new literary genres cli-fi litRPG twitterature bizarro fiction new sincerity autofiction

annotations.title: Climate Fiction, or ‘Cli-Fi,’ Is the Hottest New Literary Genre - GOOD

content.text:
Yes—but with a caveat: **completely “new” literary genres are rare**. Most 21st-century genres are better understood as **newly named, newly marketable, or newly consolidated forms** built from older traditions. Still, several genres or subgenres have clearly emerged or become distinctive in this century.

### Examples of 21st-century literary genres/subgenres

**1. Climate fiction / “cli-fi”**  
Fiction centered on climate change, ecological crisis, and human futures under environmental stress. It overlaps with science fiction, literary fiction, dystopia, and eco-fiction, but the label “cli-fi” became prominent in the 2000s–2010s. Examples include works by Kim Stanley Robinson, Barbara Kingsolver, and Richard Powers. ([good.is](https://www.good.is/articles/climate-fiction-cli-fi-genre?utm_source=openai))

**2. LitRPG / GameLit**  
Fiction structured around role-playing-game mechanics: levels, stats, quests, skill trees, inventories, and progression systems. It grew strongly with online fiction platforms, gaming culture, and self-publishing. It is arguably one of the more genuinely new popular-fiction categories of the century.

**3. New Adult fiction**  
A market category focusing on protagonists roughly aged 18–29, often dealing with college, early career, sexuality, trauma, independence, and first serious relationships. It emerged especially in the 2010s, partly through romance and self-publishing communities.

**4. Bizarro fiction**  
Absurd, grotesque, surreal, often comic speculative fiction—something like cult horror, punk surrealism, weird fiction, and pop-culture satire blended together. It had roots earlier but became a recognizable publishing scene in the 2000s. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bizarro_fiction?utm_source=openai))

**5. New Weird**  
A hybrid of fantasy, horror, science fiction, and literary surrealism that rejects the tidy worldbuilding and genre conventions of traditional fantasy. It began taking shape in the late 1990s and early 2000s, so it sits right on the century boundary. China Miéville is often associated with it. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_weird?utm_source=openai))

**6. Alt-lit / internet-native literature**  
A loose 2010s literary movement associated with Tumblr, Twitter, blogs, self-publication, irony, sincerity, autofiction, minimalist prose, and digital-age alienation. It was less a formal genre than a scene or aesthetic, but it was distinctly shaped by 21st-century internet culture. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_literature?utm_source=openai))

**7. Twitterature, SMS novels, chat fiction, and other digital-native forms**  
These are works written for or through digital platforms: tweets, texts, chat logs, emails, screenshots, notifications, hyperlinks, and social-media fragments. Some are experimental literary forms; others are commercial mobile-first fiction formats. Early 21st-century experimental writing increasingly reflects phones, social media, emoji, memes, and digital interfaces. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_literature?utm_source=openai))

**8. Autofiction’s contemporary boom**  
Autofiction itself predates the 21st century, but its global literary prominence—especially in works blending memoir, novel, essay, and self-exposure—has become one of the defining literary trends of the century. Writers such as Karl Ove Knausgård, Rachel Cusk, Ben Lerner, Sheila Heti, and Annie Ernaux helped make it central to contemporary literary fiction.

### So, have new genres emerged?

**Yes, but mostly as hybrids and labels rather than wholly unprecedented inventions.**  
The most clearly 21st-century developments are those shaped by **climate anxiety, digital life, gaming culture, online publishing, and new marketing categories**. Cli-fi, LitRPG/GameLit, New Adult, alt-lit, and digital-native fiction are probably the strongest examples.
